countries.name: India
countries.summary: India's higher-education system is overseen by the Ministry of Education and its statutory regulators - the University Grants Commission for universities and degrees, the All India Council for Technical Education for technical and management programmes, and the National Medical Commission for medical education. International applicants normally enter through an institution's own international-admissions office, through the government's Study in India portal, or through a centrally administered scheme such as DASA for engineering and architecture seats at NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded technical institutes. Entry rules differ by nationality, residency status, the prior qualification held and the discipline chosen.
countries.whyStudentsChooseIt: International applicants look at India for English-taught degrees across computing, engineering, management, design, sciences, law and health disciplines, and for a single national application route: the Ministry of Education's Study in India portal issues an SII ID and lets an applicant send one profile to several participating institutes. Government-funded study places also exist through Indian Council for Cultural Relations scholarship schemes, which are applied for through Indian diplomatic missions rather than directly to a university. What an individual applicant can access depends on citizenship, residency status, how the prior qualification is assessed for equivalence, and whether the programme is attached to a national entrance test.
countries.climate: Climate varies widely by region, from alpine Himalayan conditions in the north to tropical coastal and semi-arid zones further south, with a June-to-September monsoon across most of the country.
countries.metaTitle: Study in India: Guide for International Students
countries.metaDescription: Regulators, admission routes, entrance tests, student visa and FRRO rules that international applicants should verify before applying to an Indian university.

They combine anatomy, physiology and pathology with specialist theory and supervised hospital training. Many run for three years plus an internship. Registration and recognition rules differ by profession and country.

Laboratory work is central, and most programmes end with a supervised research dissertation. Graduates move into research laboratories, biotechnology and pharmaceutical industry roles, quality and diagnostics work, or a doctoral programme.

Programmes specialise in one field, such as medical laboratory technology, medical imaging and radiology technology, anaesthesia and operation theatre technology, dialysis, clinical research or pharmacovigilance. They combine advanced theory, hospital or laboratory practice and a research dissertation, and normally last two years, although shorter postgraduate diplomas also exist. Recognition for professional practice differs by country.

Study covers crime-scene investigation, forensic chemistry and toxicology, DNA and serology, fingerprints and questioned documents, ballistics, digital forensics, and the presentation of expert evidence in court, with extensive laboratory work and a research project. It suits graduates in chemistry, life sciences, physics or forensic science. The degree normally lasts two years and leads to work in forensic laboratories, law-enforcement agencies and private investigation, or to research.

Advanced study covers bioprocess and fermentation engineering, genetic engineering, protein and enzyme technology, bioinformatics and computational biology, and biosafety and regulation, with a research dissertation in the final year. Some programmes focus on the computational side of biology. The degree normally lasts two years and prepares graduates for research, development and production roles in the biotechnology and pharmaceutical sectors or for doctoral study.

Students learn pharmaceutics, pharmaceutical chemistry, pharmacognosy, pharmacology, human anatomy and physiology, dispensing and community pharmacy practice, with practical training in a hospital or community pharmacy. Some diplomas prepare students for pharmacy in a traditional medicine system instead. The diploma usually lasts about two years. Whether it leads to registration as a pharmacist depends on the regulator in the country where the graduate intends to work, so international students should check this before applying.

Graduates work in drug development, manufacturing, quality and regulatory roles, clinical pharmacy and teaching, or continue to doctoral research.

It differs from a B.E./B.Tech by placing more weight on mathematics and computing theory and less on engineering design. Programmes last three or four years and lead to software, data and IT roles or to master's study.

Core study covers accounting, finance, marketing, organisational behaviour, human resource management, operations, business law and economics, usually followed by a specialisation such as business analytics, international business, digital marketing, finance or healthcare management, plus an internship or live project. Programmes run for three years in many systems and four years where an honours or research year is added. Graduates move into entry-level management roles or continue to an MBA or a specialist master's degree.

The syllabus covers constitutional law, contract, torts, criminal law, property, corporate law, procedure and jurisprudence, with moot courts, legal aid clinics and internships. Programmes must be recognised by the Bar Council of India for graduates to seek enrolment as advocates in India.

Indian LLM programmes are commonly one year long and allow specialisation in areas such as constitutional law, business and corporate law, international law, criminal law, intellectual property or taxation. Assessment blends taught coursework with a dissertation, and the degree is used for academic careers, research, policy work and specialist practice rather than as a route to first enrolment as an advocate.

Study covers anatomy and physiology, fundamentals of nursing, medical-surgical, community health, mental health, child health and midwifery nursing, with extensive supervised clinical placements in hospitals and community settings. The diploma usually lasts about three years. It is a lower qualification than a B.Sc. Nursing, and registration, further study and overseas recognition depend on the nursing regulators involved, which international students should confirm first.

Graduates work as clinical nurse specialists, nurse educators and nursing managers; the right to practise still depends on registration with the relevant nursing regulator.

Registration to practise as an optometrist is controlled by national regulators, so international students should check recognition where they plan to work.

courses.summary: The Bachelor of Computer Applications is an undergraduate computing degree focused on programming, software development and applied information technology rather than engineering science. Typical coursework covers programming languages, data structures, database systems, operating systems, computer networks, web and mobile development, software engineering and discrete mathematics, with electives in areas such as data science, cyber security or cloud computing. The degree usually lasts three years, or four with an honours or research year, and commonly leads to software and IT roles or to a Master of Computer Applications.

universities.name: Jamia Hamdard
universities.summary: Jamia Hamdard is a deemed-to-be university in Hamdard Nagar, New Delhi, declared under Section 3 of the UGC Act on 10 May 1989 and sponsored by the Jamia Hamdard Society. It describes itself as government-aided. It teaches pharmacy, nursing and allied health, life sciences, computing, management, law, media and social sciences, and admits international students through its Office of Foreign Students' Affairs.
universities.campusLifestyle: The prospectus describes a 94-acre campus in Hamdard Nagar with more than 11,000 students. The FSA reports more than 450 international students from about 35 countries. The campus has a modern-medicine hospital with 700 beds and a 100-bed Unani hospital, the central Hakeem Mohammed Said library, the Hamdard Archives and Research Centre, Central Instrumentation Facilities and the Hamdard Convention Centre. The whole campus is tobacco- and alcohol-free.
universities.cityProfile: Jamia Hamdard sits at Hamdard Nagar on the Mehrauli-Badarpur Road in the South East Delhi district of New Delhi (PIN 110062), inside India's national capital. All programmes on this page are taught at the Hamdard Nagar campus; the university's off-campus centre in Kannur, Kerala, runs a separate set of courses that are not covered here. International students must register with the Foreigners Regional Registration Office within two weeks of arrival, and the medical fitness examination required for admission is done at a government-recognised hospital in Delhi/NCR. Hostel places are allotted for one academic year at a time and re-allotted each July, so students should plan for a fresh allotment every year. Scholarships from the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR) are administered in New Delhi, and ICCR scholars get preference for admission and hostel places at Jamia Hamdard.
universities.practicalExposure: Health-science students train alongside the university's own hospitals: a 700-bed modern-medicine hospital and a 100-bed Unani hospital on campus. The School of Pharmaceutical Education and Research was ranked first in the NIRF 2025 Pharmacy category, and ten departments across pharmacy, life sciences, interdisciplinary sciences and engineering hold DST-FIST grants, with seven pharmacy and science departments holding UGC-SAP grants. Central Instrumentation Facilities serve research across schools. The Centre for Nutrition and Dietetics lists internships at Max, PSRI, Lok Nayak, Batra, Alshifa and National Heart Institute hospitals, Mother Dairy and the National Foundation of India. Physiotherapy and occupational therapy degrees end with a compulsory internship, and the NCAHP-aligned allied-health bachelor's degrees include a one-year internship. The Hamdard Institute of Legal Studies and Research is listed by the Bar Council of India as an approved centre for the five-year B.A. LL.B. The M.Tech Biotechnology has DBT-supported seats with a stipend for GAT-B qualifiers.
universities.hostelOverview: Jamia Hamdard runs separate boys' and girls' hostels, including JLN, Maulana Azad and Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam for men and AMHR, Ibn-e-Sina, JLN, Rabia and Razia Sultan for women, plus Scholar House. For 2026-27, foreigners pay USD 4,000 a year for an AC single room or USD 2,000 for an AC double, including mess and laundry. A refundable hostel security deposit of INR 10,000 applies. Places are allotted for one academic year and re-allotted each July. Late fees are INR 100 a day, and AC may be limited in summer because of load shedding.
universities.dietarySupport: For foreign students, hostel fees include mess and laundry charges. The prospectus lists mess charges for 10 months of the year for Indian and NRI residents (INR 30,000 for boys and INR 32,000 for girls), which shows that meals are provided through hostel messes rather than paid separately. The FSA office assigns Arabic- and Persian-speaking student volunteers at admission time to help new arrivals who are not yet fluent in English.
universities.safetyOverview: Jamia Hamdard has zero tolerance for ragging: offenders face an FIR, suspension or expulsion, and every admitted student and parent signs an anti-ragging undertaking. The whole campus is tobacco- and alcohol-free. Grievances are handled by committees formed under the UGC (Redressal of Grievances of Students) Regulations, 2023. Hostellers are liable for any damage to hostel property.
universities.studentSupport: The Office of Foreign Students' Affairs (fsa@jamiahamdard.ac.in) handles offer letters, bonafide certificates, FRRO registration guidance, the medical fitness examination, visa extensions, programme transfers and orientation, and runs an English proficiency programme. Separate deputy advisors support male and female students. ICCR scholars get preference for admission and hostel places.

faq.question: Is Jamia Hamdard a public or private university?
faq.answer: Jamia Hamdard is a deemed-to-be university declared by the Government of India under Section 3 of the UGC Act on 10 May 1989, and it appears on UGC's list of deemed universities. It is sponsored by the Jamia Hamdard Society and describes itself as government-aided, with funding from the Hamdard National Foundation, the UGC and the Government of Delhi. It is not a central or state university.

faq.question: What language are programmes taught in?
faq.answer: Programmes on this page are taught in English. The Hotel Management prospectus page states English as the medium of instruction and examination, all entrance tests are in English, and the FSA runs an English Language Foundation (remedial English) course for international students who need it. Attendance in that course counts towards exam eligibility. Unani programmes are taught in Urdu with English, and B.A. Islamic Studies selects on a CUET Urdu paper; neither is listed on this page.

faq.question: How much does it cost to study at Jamia Hamdard?
faq.answer: For 2026-27, foreign-national tuition is charged per semester and includes one-time, examination and e-governance fees. It ranges from USD 500 (most M.A. and M.Sc. programmes) and USD 750 (most bachelor's degrees and the MBA) to USD 1,250 (B.Pharm, M.Pharm and the B.Tech degrees). A USD 200 refundable library deposit is added at admission. Hostel with meals and laundry costs USD 2,000 (AC double) or USD 4,000 (AC single) a year.

faq.question: How do international students apply?
faq.answer: Apply on the admission portal using the separate foreign-national/NRI/sponsored form. The Office of Foreign Students' Affairs checks eligibility, may hold a telephone interview, and issues a Provisional Admission Offer Letter once you pay a non-refundable 20 per cent of the annual course fee. You then get a Student Visa endorsed to Jamia Hamdard, report with original certificates, pass a medical fitness test in Delhi/NCR and pay the balance.

faq.question: Do I need an entrance exam or English test?
faq.answer: It depends on the programme. The MBA's NRI/sponsored seats need no CAT, GMAT or similar score and select on group discussion and interview. The MPT and MOT use a Jamia Hamdard entrance test, and B.Sc. Nursing and most allied-health bachelor's degrees select on NEET. No IELTS or TOEFL minimum is published; the FSA may hold a telephone interview.

faq.question: Are my school or university qualifications accepted?
faq.answer: Only qualifications from boards or universities recognised as equivalent by the Association of Indian Universities (AIU) are accepted, and foreign nationals must submit an AIU equivalence certificate. If your board or university is not on AIU's list, you apply to AIU in New Delhi for the certificate and pay its fee. Admission can be cancelled later if the qualification is found not to be AIU-recognised.

faq.question: When does the academic year start?
faq.answer: Jamia Hamdard admits once a year for a session that starts in July, and hostel places are re-allotted each July. Dates for the 2027-28 foreign-national cycle had not been published at the last check. Allow time for the provisional offer, the student visa and the AIU equivalence certificate before the session starts.

faq.question: Are scholarships available for international students?
faq.answer: From the second year onward, foreign-national students can get a 25 per cent discount on that year's tuition with at least 85 per cent aggregate marks and 75 per cent attendance, or 15 per cent with at least 75 per cent marks. Both require passing all subjects at the first attempt. Students who already received a discount at admission are not eligible. ICCR scholars also get preference for admission and hostel places.

faq.question: What is Jamia Hamdard's accreditation and ranking status?
faq.answer: NAAC accredited Jamia Hamdard A+ with a CGPA of 3.41 in its fourth cycle, declared in December 2023. In NIRF 2025 (Ministry of Education) it ranks first in Pharmacy, 47th among universities, 74th overall and 87th in Management. The Bar Council of India lists its Hamdard Institute of Legal Studies and Research as approved for the five-year B.A. LL.B. up to 2026-27.

faq.question: What accommodation is available?
faq.answer: The university runs separate hostels for men and women. In 2026-27, foreigners pay USD 4,000 a year for an AC single room or USD 2,000 for an AC double, including mess and laundry, plus a refundable INR 10,000 security deposit. Places are allotted for one academic year and re-allotted each July, and seats depend on availability.

faq.question: What visa and registration steps apply?
faq.answer: You need a Student Visa endorsed to Jamia Hamdard; the university says no other endorsement is accepted for full-time study. Register with the FRRO within two weeks of arriving in India. India's Bureau of Immigration does not allow employment or business activity on a student visa. The FSA office guides FRRO registration and visa extensions.

faq.question: Can I change programme after admission?
faq.answer: Generally no. The prospectus states that an international student admitted to one course may not change course, and transfers from another Indian institution are not normally allowed. In exceptional cases, the International Student Cell may permit a change, depending on availability, eligibility and approval by the competent authority.

faq.question: How does Jamia Hamdard compare with other Delhi universities for pharmacy?
faq.answer: Jamia Hamdard is ranked first in the NIRF 2025 Pharmacy category, and its 2026-27 foreign-national fee for the B.Pharm and M.Pharm is USD 1,250 per semester. It also has on-campus hospitals and a large allied-health school. When you compare, look at the entry route: B.Pharm ranks NEET or JEE candidates first, while M.Pharm ranks GPAT candidates first.

evidence.claimText: The University Grants Commission is the statutory body of the Government of India for coordination, determination and maintenance of standards of higher education, operating under the Ministry of Education.
evidence.sourceLabel: University Grants Commission (UGC) - official site
evidence.internalNotes: UGC publishes the authoritative lists of Central, State, Deemed-to-be and State Private universities, plus a published list of fake universities. Corroborated by the Study in India portal Indian Higher Education page, which states all institutions are governed by the Ministry of Education.

evidence.claimText: The All India Council for Technical Education is the Government of India statutory body for technical education, covering engineering, management and allied technical programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) - official site

evidence.claimText: The National Medical Commission is the Government of India regulator for medical education and medical institutions; medical and dental admission is governed separately from general higher education.
evidence.sourceLabel: National Medical Commission (NMC) - official site

evidence.claimText: India's higher-education landscape includes over 1,100 universities and more than 45,000 colleges, all governed by the Ministry of Education, and higher education begins after 12 years of schooling.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Indian Higher Education
evidence.internalNotes: Portal-published counts are approximate and shift between AISHE cycles; treat them as indicative and re-check at review. Regulator identity is separately verified against UGC and AICTE.

evidence.claimText: The Study in India portal is the Government of India route for international applicants: the applicant registers for a compulsory SII ID, explores participating institutes and courses, submits applications to several institutes from one profile, accepts an offer letter, then applies for a student visa or student e-visa.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - official portal

evidence.claimText: The Bureau of Immigration directs foreign nationals who wish to apply to Indian institutes to register under the Study in India scheme, confirming the portal as a government-recognised route rather than a third-party service.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: The Indian Council for Cultural Relations administers Government of India scholarship schemes for international students at UG, PG and PhD level, including AYUSH streams; applications are handled through the ICCR A2A scholarship portal and the applicant's Indian diplomatic mission.
evidence.sourceLabel: ICCR Admissions to Alumni (A2A) Scholarship Portal
evidence.internalNotes: Portal states that applicants should contact the Indian Mission for scholarship updates - eligibility and open cycles are mission-specific and vary by country, so no scheme may be presented as open to all nationalities.

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals must obtain a Student Visa to pursue on-campus, full-time structured courses or research at educational institutions recognised by the Government of India. Student (S-3) visas cover yoga, Vedic culture, Indian dance, music and Buddhist studies at approved institutions; Student (S-5) visas cover internships.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals entering India on a Student visa valid for more than 180 days must register with the jurisdictional FRRO or FRO within 14 days of arrival. Pakistani nationals must register within 24 hours. Children under 12 years and OCI cardholders are exempt from registration, and citizens of Nepal and Bhutan are exempt from both visa and registration requirements.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Registration Requirements
evidence.internalNotes: Corroborated by the Study in India Onboarding & FRRO page, which states e-FRRO registration within 14 days of landing. Nationality-dependent rule - never state one universal deadline.

evidence.claimText: Students on an Indian Student visa must not undertake employment or business activity in India, must open a Non-Resident Ordinary (NRO) account with a recognised Indian bank and furnish the details to the FRRO, and must not enrol in off-campus franchise centres, distance-learning study centres of open universities or outreach programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India
evidence.internalNotes: Directly constrains any work-rights or earn-while-you-study claim on India pages. Do not publish part-time work guidance for India.

evidence.claimText: An applicant should possess proof of admission to a full-time regular academic course at a recognised Indian institution and evidence of financial support, and must also hold a No Objection Certificate from the Ministry of Health where the admission is to a medical or paramedical course.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Onboarding & FRRO
evidence.internalNotes: The portal adds its own disclaimer that document requirements differ across countries and must be confirmed with the nearest Indian embassy.

evidence.claimText: Admission for Foreign Nationals, OCIs, PIOs and NRIs to undergraduate engineering, architecture and planning programmes at NITs, IIEST, IIITs, SPAs and other centrally funded technical institutes runs through the Ministry of Education DASA scheme, and for the 2026-27 year admission is on the basis of JEE (Main) 2026. DASA seats are supernumerary and capped at up to 15 per cent of a programme's total seats. IITs are outside the DASA scheme.
evidence.sourceLabel: Information Brochure DASA 2026 (UG), Central Seat Allocation Board / Ministry of Education
evidence.internalNotes: The qualifying-exam basis has changed between cycles (SAT in earlier cycles, JEE Main for 2026-27). Never state the accepted exam without naming the admission year. Corroborated by dasanit.org, which describes DASA as an MoE scheme for Foreign Nationals, PIOs, OCIs and NRIs to NITs, CFTIs and other premier technical institutions other than IITs.

evidence.claimText: Non-Resident Indians, Overseas Citizens of India and Foreign Nationals are eligible to appear in NEET (UG) and are eligible for admission to medical and dental colleges subject to the rules of the respective State Governments, institutions and the Government of India. Foreign applicants must upload documentary proof of nationality with the application and are directed to confirm eligibility with the competent state and counselling authorities.
evidence.sourceLabel: Information Bulletin NEET (UG)-2026, National Testing Agency
evidence.internalNotes: Chapter 6, sections 1-2. No India medical page may present a NEET-free route. Eligibility is explicitly conditional on state and institution rules, so it varies by college.

evidence.claimText: The National Assessment and Accreditation Council, established in 1994 as an autonomous institution of the UGC, assesses and accredits Indian higher education institutions. The National Institutional Ranking Framework, launched by the Ministry of Education in September 2015, is the government ranking framework for Indian institutions.
evidence.sourceLabel: NAAC - official site
evidence.internalNotes: NIRF corroborated separately at https://www.nirfindia.org/Home (MoE, launched 29 September 2015). Use a NAAC grade or NIRF rank only with the assessment or ranking year stated.

evidence.claimText: The UGC publishes a list of fake universities alongside its lists of Central, State, Deemed-to-be and State Private universities, so institutional recognition must be checked against UGC records before an Indian institution is presented as degree-awarding.
evidence.sourceLabel: University Grants Commission - Higher Education Institutions listings
evidence.internalNotes: Operational rule for this catalogue: no Indian university is published without a verifiable UGC listing and, where applicable, AICTE approval or NMC recognition.

evidence.claimText: India spans Himalayan, tropical coastal, semi-arid and monsoon-affected climate zones, with the southwest monsoon typically running from June to September.
evidence.sourceLabel: India Meteorological Department, Ministry of Earth Sciences
evidence.internalNotes: General climatic framing only; do not present city-level weather claims at country level.
